data.description:
## Description

What: New CI test under plugins/dso/tests/ that scans every .sh file under plugins/dso/ for 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' invocations and fails the build when any such invocation appears outside pr-destructive-action.sh itself; SKILL.md files are explicitly excluded from the scan. Why: Static build-time enforcement complements the runtime hook and prevents new direct-call regressions in shell code. Scope IN: the scanner test with .sh-only scope; explicit exclusion of pr-destructive-action.sh (the legitimate site) and of SKILL.md files; a positive test (a planted direct call fails the scan) and a negative test (a wrapper-routed call passes). Scope OUT: SKILL.md behavioral compliance (enforced by the runtime hook, draft-5).


## Done Definitions

- A CI test scans every .sh under plugins/dso/ and fails when 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' appears in any .sh other than pr-destructive-action.sh ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The scan excludes SKILL.md files (and other non-.sh prose) so script-name mentions in instruction text do not trigger false positives ← Satisfies: sc-5
- A positive fixture (planted direct gh pr close in a throwaway .sh) makes the scan fail, and a negative fixture (wrapper-routed call) passes ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The CI scan ships in warn/advisory mode (reports direct gh pr destructive call sites but does NOT fail the build) and is flipped to fail-the-build only after draft-7 migrates the merge-to-main-pr.sh call sites (lines 437/549/1295); a test asserts that in warn mode a pre-migration direct call is reported-but-non-fatal, and that the enforce flip fails the build on a planted direct call — so the scan never self-deadlocks the merge pipeline before migration lands ← Satisfies: sc-5

## Considerations

- [Harness] 7510-0198: coordinate the plugins/dso/tests/ CI grep-test layout to share the scanner harness with epic 7510-0198's R2 structural-enforcement scan rather than duplicating it.
- [Scope] 2239-1545: the scan targets .sh only, isolating runtime-portability concerns to the hook implementation; do not broaden the scan to non-.sh files.
- [Self-exclude] pr-destructive-action.sh is the one legitimate site containing gh pr <action>; the scan must exclude it precisely (by path, not by a fragile inline marker).
- [No-self-deadlock] Do NOT add depends_on draft-7 to draft-6 — draft-7 depends on draft-6, so that edge would create a cycle. Instead the scan is non-enforcing (warn/advisory) until draft-7 migrates merge-to-main-pr.sh:437/549/1295, then flipped to fail-the-build. This prevents the scan from redding CI on the un-migrated merge pipeline (self-deadlock).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want a CI test that scans every .sh under plugins/dso/ for direct gh pr destructive invocations outside the wrapper, so that the single-permitted-path invariant is enforced at build time and regressions are caught before merge.
